entries.toelichting: Proper noun ('lightning'); judge of Naphtali, captain with Deborah against Sisera; concordantly transliterated (distinguished from baraq-noun 'lightning').
Head of a Nethinim-family in the return-list - Ezra 2:53, Nehemiah 7:55.
Judg-he-took-thorns-of-the-wilderness-and-briers-and-with-them-he-taught-the-men-of-Succoth and Judg-he-broke-down-the-tower-of-Penuel (Judg 8:7,16). Hyphenated.
Gemstone row 1 breastplate (lightning-stone); Ex 28:17.
Second-sense bareqet as-gemstone Tyre-king; Eze 28:13.
Qal/Niphal: make pure, sift, choose-out; concordantly 'purify'.
Proper noun, king of Gomorrah; Gen 14:2; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Birsha.
Patronym-clan David's-warrior Naharai; 1Chr 11:39; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Berothite.
Besor-brook where David's-weary-men-stayed (1Sam 30:9,10,21). English convention: Besor. 'Cool-brook' or 'good-stream'.
Good message of victory or royal favour (2Sam 4:10; 18:20,22,25,27; 2Kgs 7:9). Hyphenated to preserve the joyful-tidings-aspect; family with H1319 basar 'bring-good-news'.
Piel: bring food to readiness in water; distinguished from tsalah (roast) and afah (bake); concordantly 'boil'.
Ex-eat-not-raw-or-boiled-in-water-but-roasted-in-fire and Num-priest's-son-shall-offer-not-shall-he-eat-boiled-meat (Ex 12:9; Num 6:19 cf). Hyphenated.
Persian-administrator Ezra 4:7 letter-to-Artaxerxes; possibly in-peace-official.
Bridegroom-eats-honey-with-balsam; Song 5:1.
From √basam (smell pleasantly); fragrant spice, balsam; the hyphenated English marks the aromatic load.
Wife of Esau and daughter of Solomon (Gen 26:34; 36:3,4,10,13,17; 1Kgs 4:15). 'Fragrant'. English convention: Basemath.
Proper noun (region east of Jordan); fertile plateau; concordantly transliterated.
Samaria's-calf-to-Assyria as-shame; Hos 10:6.
Polel; poor-trodden-underfoot; Amos 5:11.
Piel: announce victory or salvation, bring-evangel; the hyphenated English distinguishes from basar noun 'flesh'.
Unique lexeme. Anatomical and generic ('all flesh' = all living). 'Flesh' covers both.
Aramaic word for flesh or body - in Daniel 4:12 (of his fruits all flesh was fed) and Daniel 7:5 (devour much flesh); parallel of Hebrew basar.
From √bosh (be-ashamed); the feeling and the cause of shame; concordantly 'shame'.
Root bnh (build, H1129); female counterpart of ben (H1121a). 'Daughter' standard.
Large liquid-measure (about 22 litres), counterpart of ephah for dry measures; the hyphenated English distinguishes from bat 'daughter'.
The bath-capacity-measure for liquids in the Aramaic context - Ezra 7:22 (a hundred baths of wine, a hundred baths of oil); Aramaic cognate of Hebrew bath (about 22 litres).
Vineyard-shall-become-cut-off-field; Isa 5:6.
Enemy-swarms rest in chasm-clefts; Isa 7:19.
Son of Nahor and Milcah, nephew-of-Abraham, father-of-Rebekah-and-Laban - link in Patriarch-genealogy (Gen 22:22-23, 24:15,24,47,50, 25:20, 28:2,5).
Second-sense Bethuel as place Simeon-city; 1Chr 4:30; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, Simeon-city; Josh 19:4; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bethul.
Woman who has not yet had relations; distinguished from naarah (young-woman general); concordantly 'virgin'.
Plural-abstract of betulah (virgin, H1330); state-or-tokens-of-virginity (Lev 21:13 high-priest 'wife in-her-virginity takes', Deut 22:14-15,17,20 'tokens-of-virginity').
Proper noun, Egyptian Pharaoh-daughter wife of Mered; 1Chr 4:18; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bithiah.
Piel; enemies-shall-Zion with-swords-hew-through; Eze 16:40.
Gen-Abram-took-all-the-animals-and-divided-them-in-the-middle and Gen-the-birds-he-did-not-divide and Jer-cut-the-covenant-calf-in-two (Gen 15:10 twice; Jer 34:18). Hyphenated.

Mountains-of-Bether or division-mountains in Song-of-Songs and covenant-sacrifice-pieces Abraham (Gen 15:10; Jer 34:18,19; Song 2:17). English convention: Bether-mountains. 'Divided-pieces' (cleaving-sacrifice).
Proper noun, Cleft-mountains where bride calls to bridegroom; Song 2:17; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bether.
Proper noun Heshbon-gate 'daughter-of-multitudes'; Song 7:4; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bath-rabbim.
Proper noun, region near Mahanaim; 2Sam 2:29; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bithron.
Compound-name 'daughter-of-seven/oath' - wife-of David after-adultery and-death-of Uriah, mother-of-Solomon (2Sam 11:3, 1Kgs 1:11-31, 2:13-19).
Proper noun variant Bathsheba wife of David; 1Chr 3:5; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bath-shua.
Moab is haughty and proud; Isa 16:6.
Swelling-rising of water, pride or God's might (Ex 15:1,21; Job 8:11; 10:16; Eze 47:5). Hyphenated to preserve the physical-swelling-motion; root of H1343 ge'eh 'proud-haughty'.
High-lifted-self-exalting (adjective) (Job 40:11,12; Ps 94:2; 123:4; 140:6; Prov 15:25; 16:19; Isa 2:12; Jer 48:29). Hyphenated to distinguish attitude-quality from H2086 zed 'insolent'.
YHWH-hates pride-and-arrogance; Prov 8:13.
Proper noun, spy of Gad; Num 13:15; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Geuel.
From √gaah (be-high); proud attitude as sin (positive = majesty); concordantly 'haughtiness'.
From √gaah (be-high); positively exaltation, negatively pride; concordantly 'exaltation'.
Majestic exalted-loftiness of God or sea-waves (Ps 17:10; 68:35; Isa 9:18; 12:5; 26:10; 28:1,3; Job 41:7). Hyphenated to distinguish divine-loftiness from H1346 ga'avah 'pride'.
Our-soul is filled with mocking of proud-men; Ps 123:4.
Root g'l. Family-duty: redeem from debt, slavery, or blood-feud. 'Redeem' preserves the family-juridical loosing-action; 'rescue' clashes with yasha (H3467).
Second-sense gaal; year-of-my-redeemed has-come; Isa 63:4.
Second homonym of gaal (redeemer H1350); Niphal/Pual/Hithpael/Hiphil: ritual-physical defile/make-unclean with blood or filth (Lam 4:14, Isa 59:3, Mal 1:7,12, Dan 1:8, Zeph 3:1).
Pual-passive; priests who polluted priesthood-covenant; Neh 13:29.
From √gaal (redeem); right and price of kinsman-redemption (Lev 25, Ruth); the hyphenated English marks family-juridical nature.
Vaulted top (back, vault, eyebrow, rim), edge-elevation; the hyphenated English marks the bow-shaped top.
Aramaic; Dan 7:6; parallel to Hebrew gab.
2K-thus-says-the-LORD-make-this-valley-full-of-trenches and Jer-her-pits-are-filled-with-water (2K 3:16; Jer 14:3). Hyphenated.
Second-sense gev; cedar-ceiling-panels; 1Kgs 6:9.
People-fall-on-spoil like locusts; Isa 33:4.
Aramaic-specific term for-dug-pit-for-lions - exclusively in Dan 6:8,13,17-18,20-21,24-25,27 'lions-den' into which Daniel-was-cast for-prayer-against-decree of-Darius.
2S-there-was-again-a-battle-at-Gob-with-the-Philistines-then-Sibbecai-smote and 2S-there-was-again-a-battle-at-Gob-with-the-Philistines (2S 21:18,19). Hyphenated.
Water-pool or drinking-pool - in Isaiah 30:14 (to take water out of a pit) and Ezekiel 47:11 (the marshy places and her pits); concrete rain-pool in mountain-region.
Qal: be elevated; Hiphil: lift up; negatively: be haughty; the hyphenated English marks state.
1Sam-Saul-tall-of-shoulder-above-people and Ps-righteous-God-exalted and Prov-haughty-pride-of-heart (1Sam 16:7; Ps 138:6; Prov 16:5). Hyphenated.
From √gavah (be-high); elevated dimension, haughtiness; the hyphenated English distinguishes from marom.
Adjective from √gavah; elevated in dimension or status; concordantly 'high'.
Haughty loftiness - in Isaiah 2:11 (the lofty looks of man shall be humbled and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down) and Isaiah 2:17 (the loftiness of man shall be bowed down).
Unique lexeme. Border or border-region. 'Border-territory' preserves both the line and the adjacent zone; 'border' alone is too narrow.
Female parallel-form of gevul (border-territory, H1366); demarcation-line-or-territory specifically in-inheritance-division (Num 32:33).
Root gbr (be-strong, H1396). Substantively 'mighty-man', adjectivally 'strong'. 'Strong-mighty-man' preserves both fields; 'hero' alone is too narrow, 'strong' too abstract.
From √gavar (be-strong); might-deed/strength-manifestation; the hyphenated English marks 'strength-as-action'.
Aramaic parallel to gevurah; God's-wisdom-and-strength; Dan 2:20.
Bald at temples-forehead-part; Lev 13:41.
Front-side-bald of head or clothing (Lev 13:42,43,55). Hyphenated to distinguish front-baldness from H7146 qarachath 'rear-baldness' and H4696 metsach 'forehead'.
Proper noun, Benjamite Jerusalem-inhabitant; Neh 11:8; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gabbai.
Proper noun, place on Assyrian-march-route; Isa 10:31; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gebim.
Large drinking-bowl (Joseph's silver goblet, lamp-cups of menorah); concordantly 'goblet'.
Gen-Jacob-as-lord-over-brothers-Isaac-blesses and Gen-I-have-set-you-lord-over-him (Gen 27:29,37). Hyphenated to distinguish lord-master-ruler-aspect from H113 adon 'lord'.
Commanding-female title, often for mother of reigning king (1Kgs 11:19; 15:13; 2Kgs 10:13; 2Chr 15:16; Jer 13:18; 29:2). Hyphenated to preserve court-power-aspect; family with H1376 gebir.
Wisdom not-to-be-compared with crystals; Job 28:18.
Border-trace around territory or mountain (Ex 19:12,23; Deut 19:14; Josh 18:20; Zech 9:2). Hyphenated to preserve the border-demarcation-aspect; family with H1366 gevul 'border-territory'.
Proper noun Byblos-city-suppliers Tyre; Eze 27:9; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gebal.
Proper noun, people in coalition against Israel; Ps 83:7; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gebal.
Inhabitant of Gebal-Byblos; Josh 13:5; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Giblite.
Breastplate-chain-fastening; Ex 28:22.
Crooked-backed priest excluded; Lev 21:20.
Human formed from-milk-to-cheese womb-comparison; Job 10:10.
Humped mountain-tops or elevated summits - in Psalm 68:16 (why do you leap, you many-peaked mountains?) and 68:17 (the mountain that God desired for his abode); only in plural, from gav-arched-top.
Proper noun ('hill'); city in Benjamin, Levite-city; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, city founded by Sheva-Caleb; 1Chr 2:49; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gibea.
Rounded elevation, smaller than har (mountain); concordantly 'hill'.
Proper noun ('hill'); city in Benjamin, residence of Saul; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun ('hill-city'); city of the Gibeonites; concordantly transliterated.
Flax-bloom-stalk; seventh plague; Ex 9:31.
Inhabitant of Gibeon, Hivite city (2Sam 21:1,2,3,4,9; Neh 3:7; 1Chr 12:4). Gentilic; family with H1391 Giv'on.
Proper noun, Benjamin-city; Josh 18:28; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gibeath.
Patronym-clan David's-warriors Gibeah-Benjamin; 1Chr 12:3; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gibeathite.
Qal: have the upper hand, show oneself mighty; the hyphenated English marks comparative state.
From √gavar (be-strong); adult male as powerful person; distinguished from ish (man-human); the hyphenated English preserves strength-connotation.
Father of Solomon-officer 1Kgs 4:19; possibly compound with H1127 Ben-Geber.
With strong-perfect, perfect-be YHWH; Ps 18:25.
Aramaic noun: adult man; parallel to Hebrew gever; concordantly compound with language-marker.
Aramaic parallel to gibbor; warriors to bind-men; Dan 3:20.
Proper noun, origin-group of returnees; Ezra 2:20; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gibbar.
Proper noun archangel explains-Daniel-vision; Dan 8:16; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gabriel.
Mistress-over-handmaid; also city-queen as metaphor (Gen 16:4,8,9; 2Kgs 5:3; Ps 123:2; Prov 30:23; Isa 24:2; 47:5,7). Hyphenated to distinguish female-ruler-status from H4436 malkah.
Levitical city in Dan, besieged by Israel (Josh 19:44; 21:23; 1Kgs 15:27; 16:15,17). English convention: Gibbethon.
Flat-built roof as additional living-space; the hyphenated English marks construction.
Ex-manna-was-as-coriander-seed-white and Num-manna-was-like-coriander-seed (Ex 16:31; Num 11:7). Hyphenated.
Proper noun Babylonian-deity of fortune; Isa 65:11; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gad.
Gen-Leah-fortune-comes-named-him-Gad and Isa-who-set-table-for-Gad-fortune-god (Gen 30:11; Isa 65:11). Hyphenated.
Proper noun (son/tribe of Israel); concordantly transliterated.
Aramaic loanword for treasurer or treasury-keeper - in Daniel 3:2 (the treasurers) and Daniel 3:3 (the treasurers); Persian ganzabara, official at Dura-plain-ceremonial.
Deut-they-journeyed-from-Moserah-to-Gudgodah and Deut-and-from-Gudgodah-to-Jotbathah-a-land-of-water-streams (Deut 10:7). Hyphenated.
Ritual self-cutting at mourning or at Baal-worship (Deut 14:1; 1Kgs 18:28; Jer 5:7; 16:6; 41:5; 47:5; 48:37; Mic 4:14). Hyphenated to mark middle-reflexive action.
Aramaic verb for hewing down or felling - in Daniel 4:14 (hew down this tree) and Daniel 4:23 (hew down this tree); imperative in angel-decree to Nebuchadnezzar-tree.
Jordan-bank-overflowing at high-water (Josh 3:15; 4:18; 1Chr 12:15; Isa 8:7). Hyphenated to distinguish the bank-edge-aspect from H7097 qatseh 'end' and H8193 safah 'edge-lip'.
Armed gang or military detachment; concordantly 'raiding-band'.
Moab-mourns-with-cutting in hands; Jer 48:37.
Furrow-ploughed-field God-soaks-earth; Ps 65:10.
Root gdl (be-great, H1431). 'Great' is direct equivalent.
Second-sense gadol as personal-name father of Zabdiel priest; Neh 11:14; concordantly transliterated.
Female abstract of gadol (great, H1419a); state-or-action-of-being-made-great distinguished from godel (greatness-inward, H1433) (2Sam 7:21 = 1Chr 17:19).
Isa-reproaches-they-heard and Zeph-their-reviling-and-mockery and Eze-rebuked-and-reproached (Isa 43:28; 51:7; Zeph 2:8; Eze 5:15). Hyphenated.
People-as-scorn and mockery among-peoples; Eze 5:15.
Young of goat, edible feast-offering; the hyphenated English marks age.
2K-then-Menahem-the-son-of-Gadi-went-up-from-Tirzah and 2K-Menahem-the-son-of-Gadi-became-king-over-Israel (2K 15:14,17). Hyphenated.
From pn Gad; member of tribe Gad; the hyphenated English marks ethnicity.
Proper noun, spy of Manasseh; Num 13:11; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gaddi.
Proper noun, spy of Zebulon; Num 13:10; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gaddiel.
Swollen-Jordan-banks over which Gad-warriors went; 1Chr 12:15.
Bride-follows-goats to shepherds-tents; Song 1:8.
Burning-in-standing-grain-sheaves and Job's-haystack-image (Ex 22:6; Job 5:26; 21:32). Hyphenated.
Hapax Job 21:32 grave-mound-watched; sub-sense pair with H1430a wheat-stack same stack-form.
Root gdl. Stative 'become-great'; causative 'make-great'. 'Become-great' preserves stative kernel; derived gadol (H1419a).
Child-in-growth-stage before adulthood (Gen 26:13; 1Sam 2:26; 2Chr 17:12). Hyphenated to distinguish growing-youth-aspect from H1431 gadal 'become-great' and H5288 na'ar 'youth'.
From √gdl (be-great); abstract noun 'greatness/magnitude' (Deut 3:24 'Your greatness', Eze 31:7 'greatness of branches'); concordantly 'greatness'.
Deut-twisted-cords-shall-you-make-on-the-four-corners-of-your-cloak and 1K-and-the-nets-were-made-also-right-and-left-twisted-works-for-the-capitals (Deut 22:12; 1K 7:17). Hyphenated.
Post-exilic-Nethinim-family-ancestor and Solomon-servant-family-head (Ezra 2:47,56; Neh 7:49,58). English convention: Giddel. 'Made-great'; family with H1431 gadal 'be-great'.
Pre-exilic persons of the same name as the governor (1Chr 25:3,9; Ezra 10:18; Jer 38:1; Zeph 1:1). 'YHWH-is-great'. English convention: Gedaliah; distinguished from H1436b Gedaliah (longer form).
Proper noun ('YHWH-is-great'); governor over Judah after fall of Jerusalem; concordantly transliterated.
1Chr-Hananiah-Hanani-Eliathah-Giddalti-and-Romamti-Ezer and 1Chr-the-twenty-second-Giddalti (1Chr 25:4,29). Hyphenated.
Qal/Piel: hew off (horns, tree, idol-image); concordantly 'cut-down'.
Proper noun ('hewer'); judge from Manasseh; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, place where Israel defeated Benjamin-fugitives; Judg 20:45; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gidom.
Benjamite father of Abidan (Num 1:11; 2:22; 7:60,65; 10:24). English convention: Gideoni. 'Hewer'.
Words of contempt or blasphemy utter (Num 15:30; 2Kgs 19:6,22; Ps 44:17; Isa 37:6,23; Eze 20:27). Hyphenated to mark verbal-reproach.
Qal/Piel: with-wall-or-hedge enclose (Num 32:16,24,36, Job 19:8, Ps 89:41, Prov 24:31, Hos 2:8, Amos 9:11, Mic 7:11). Hyphenated.
Second-sense geder; wall-stones-fallen-down sluggard's-field; Prov 24:31.
Proper noun, Canaanite place; Josh 12:13; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Geder.
Town-name from Judah's lowland (Josh 12:13; 15:36; 1Chr 4:18; 12:5; 27:28; 1Kgs 4:10). English convention: Geder.
Low dry-built stone-fence for-vineyard or-pasture-field distinguished from chomah (city-wall, H2346) by agricultural-border-aspect (Num 22:24, Ps 62:4, 80:13, Prov 24:31, Eze 13:5, 22:30, 42:7,10).
Female form of gader (stone-wall) with specifically-functional meaning as-sheep-pen-stall (Num 32:16,24,36, 1Sam 24:4, Zeph 2:6).
Proper noun, Judah-city lowland; Josh 15:36; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gederah.

Josh-Zenan-Hadashah-Migdal-gad-Dilan-Mizpeh-Joktheel-Lachish-Bozkath-Eglon-Cabbon-Lahmas-Cithlish-Gederoth and 2Chr-Philistines-attacked-cities-in-lowland-and-South-of-Judah-and-took-Beth-shemesh-Aijalon (Josh 15:41; 2Chr 28:18). Hyphenated.
Gentilic from Gedera (1Chr 27:28 Baal-Hanan-David's-officer); from H1445 Gedera-city.
Proper noun, Judah-city lowland; Josh 15:36; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gederothaim.
Hapax-form; 'this-is-the-border' tribal-division; Eze 47:13.
Qal; no-healing for Ephraim's-wound; Hos 5:13.
Cheerful-heart gives-medicine; Prov 17:22.
Elijah-bow-down-pray-Carmel and Elisha-stretch-himself-on-dead-child (1Kgs 18:42; 2Kgs 4:34,35). Hyphenated to distinguish bow-down-stoop-crouch-aspect from H7812 shachah 'bow-down-worship'.
YHWH-behind-back-cast and psalm-behind-back-law-cast and sinner-Job's-back (1Kgs 14:9; Neh 9:26; Isa 38:17). Hyphenated.
Aramaic form for 'inside/midst'; furnace-midst (Dan 3:6,11,15,21,23-26), lions'-den-midst (Dan 6:7,12,16-17,24), visions 'in the midst of the night' (Dan 7:15).
Back- or body-middle as target of strokes (Prov 10:13; 19:29; 26:3; Isa 38:17; 50:6). Hyphenated to distinguish back-side-aspect from homonym H1460b gev-II 'inside'.
Hapax Job 30:5 body-people-driven-out; sub-sense pair with H1460a back same root.
Remaining-farmers of poorest class; 2Kgs 25:12.
Nineveh-leaders as locust-swarms fleeing-away; Nah 3:17.
Locust as plague-creature - in Amos 7:1 (the former of locusts in the beginning of the late-growth) and Nahum 3:17 (your princes are as locusts); distinguished from H1462a gov-I (great-heap).

Reubenite (1Chr 5:4) and apocalyptic-enemy in eschatological-prophecy - Eze 38:2,3,14,16,18, 39:1,11,15 'set your-face against Gog of-land-Magog prince-of-Rosh-Meshech-Tubal' - future-great-onslaught.
Raiding-bands against Gad-wordplay (Gen 49:19 three times). Hyphenated to distinguish raid-press-overcome-aspect from H6555 parats 'break-through' (already assigned).
Arrow-from-back-drawn-out at wicked-death; Job 20:25.
Lowly-bowed-deliver-by-pride-laying-down and Job-man-from-his-pride-laying-aside and Jer-heart-pride-disciplined (Job 22:29; 33:17; Jer 13:17). Hyphenated.
Aramaic parallel to gaavah; in-pride-walking humble; Dan 4:37.
Num-wind-brought-quail-from-sea and Ps-you-have-passed-his-life-quickly (Num 11:31; Ps 90:10). Hyphenated to distinguish sweep-bring-pass-over-aspect from H1494 gazaz 'shear'.
Gen-Abraham-took-three-year-heifer-three-year-goat-and-ram-and-turtledove-and-young-pigeon and Deut-as-eagle-fluttering-over-young (Gen 15:9; Deut 32:11). Hyphenated.
River and region to which Israel was deported (2Kgs 17:6; 18:11; 19:12; 1Chr 5:26; Isa 37:12). English convention: Gozan.

Root gwh. Political-territorial entity. To be distinguished from am (H5971a, people as common-descent). 'Nation' preserves that distinction; 'gentile/heathen' is a later cultural choice that breaks concordance.
Gen-Tidal-king-Goyim and Gen-same-coalition-Tidal-Goyim and Josh-king-Goyim-of-Gilgal-one (Gen 14:1,9; Josh 12:23). Hyphenated.
Body (living or as corpse), fig. mummy; the hyphenated English marks dead or unanimated dimension.
From √galah (carry-away); both the state and the group of exiles; concordantly 'exile'.
Bashanite city-of-refuge for manslayers (Deut 4:43; Josh 20:8; 21:27; 1Chr 6:71). English convention: Golan.
Hapax Eccl 10:8 digger-pit-falls-in; possibly loan of uncertain origin.
Naphtali-son and Gad-family (Gen 46:24; Num 26:48; 1Chr 5:15; 7:13). English convention: Guni. 'Protected'.
Patronym-clan son of Naphtali; Num 26:48; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gunite.
Qal: undergo death-struggle, expire; the hyphenated English marks the moment of life-end.
Hiphil; Jerusalem-gates bolted on time; Neh 7:3.
1Chr-and-they-took-his-body-and-his-sons-and-brought-them-to-Jabesh and 1Chr-and-they-buried-their-bones-under-the-oak-near-Jabesh (1Chr 10:12,12). Hyphenated.
Root gwr. Temporarily dwell as stranger. 'Sojourn' preserves the temporary stranger-status; derived ger (H1616).
Throng-together in fear or against someone (Ps 56:7; 59:4; Isa 54:15; Hos 7:14). Hyphenated; distinguishes group-gathering from homonym H1481a gur 'sojourn'.
Third homonym distinguished from gur-I (sojourn, H1481a) and gur-II (raise-strife, H1481b); Qal: anxiously-shrink-back-from (Num 22:3, Deut 1:17, 18:22, 32:27, Ps 22:24, 33:8).
Lion-or jackal-whelp (Gen 49:9; Deut 33:22; Jer 51:38; Eze 19:2,3,5; Lam 4:3; Nah 2:13). Hyphenated to mark suckling-young; distinguished from homonyms H1481a 'sojourn' and H1481b 'band-together'.
Proper noun, place where Ahaziah was wounded; 2Kgs 9:27; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gur.
Babel-princes-roar like-lion-whelps; Jer 51:38.
Proper noun, place of Arabs whom Uzziah defeated; 2Chr 26:7; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gur-Baal.
Unique lexeme. Dice-event, allotted portion. 'Lot' covers both the means and the outcome.
The earth-clods under which Job's skin is swollen - Job 7:5 (my skin is broken and become loathsome) and figuratively the bodies of the dying who return to dust.
Wool-shearing-firstfruits-priest and king-shearing and Gideon-fleece and king-mowing-portion (Deut 18:4; Amos 7:1; Ps 72:6). Hyphenated.
Persian loanword for treasury-keeper; Ezra 1:8.
Aramaic parallel to Hebrew gizbar; Persian empire-financiers; Ezra 7:21.
Qal-participle; God-brought-me-out-of-mother's-womb; Ps 71:6.
